handbookNote: Wyoming Real Estate Broker license exam. Part of the 2026-09-03 R26 population-tier broker buildout (population order: UT > NV > IA > AR > KS > MS > ID > NE > WV > HI > NH > MT > RI > DE > SD > ND > AK > VT > WY -- WY is the final state in this tier). Exam vendor: Pearson VUE, under contract with the Wyoming Real Estate Commission (WREC) (Candidate Handbook #095100, national outline effective 4/1/2025, state outline effective 1/1/2021). National/General portion: 80 scored items + 5 unscored pretest, 2.5 hours. Wyoming State portion: 50 scored items for Broker (vs. 40 for Salesperson), 1.5 hours. Passing score is a SCALED score of 75 (0-100 scale, NOT raw percent-correct), National and State scored/passed INDEPENDENTLY (retake only the failed portion, within 6 months). track_registry models this as exam_question_count=130, exam_duration_sec=14400, pass_percent=75, min_correct=98 (round(130*0.75)), same scaled-score/independent-retake convention as UT/NV/KS/ID/NE/WV/MT/RI/DE in this campaign. NATIONAL/GENERAL PORTION (80 items, 8 sections) reuses the exact same real Pearson VUE national item bank as Utah/Nevada/Kansas/Idaho/Nebraska/West Virginia/Montana/Rhode Island/Delaware/Alaska -- Wyoming's own Broker outline weights are IDENTICAL (10/8/10/15/12/9/8/8 across the same 8 sections). WYOMING STATE PORTION (50 items, real Broker item-count RANGES -- W.S. 33-28-107(a) mandates the Broker exam be 'more exacting... and more stringent' than Salesperson's): The Real Estate Licensing Agency's Powers (2-5, real $2,500 max administrative fine per offense under W.S. 33-28-111(a), independent hearing-officer process under the Wyoming APA), Licensing (4-6, real 3-year renewal cycle with a statutory 60-hour CE ceiling under W.S. 33-28-118 though WREC's own current rule sets it lower -- 45 hrs for Salesperson/Associate Broker, 53 hrs for Responsible Broker), Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees (14-16, incl. Wyoming's real, distinctive 'designated licensee' mechanism -- different licensees at the same firm can represent opposing sides without that alone constituting dual agency, subject to mandatory transaction-manager appointment and a confidentiality wall (W.S. 33-28-102(b)(xv), 302(h)/(j)) -- and Wyoming's separate non-agent, non-fiduciary 'intermediary' brokerage status (W.S. 33-28-305)), Additional Topics (11-13, incl. the real Recovery Fund under W.S. 33-28-201-206 with a $10,000 max-per-claim cap (33-28-202(a)), Wyoming's genuinely distinctive TWO-MERIDIAN PLSS land-description system -- the 6th Principal Meridian statewide except the Wind River Meridian (established 1875) for the Wind River area -- and Wyoming's real nonjudicial foreclosure-by-advertisement process with an unusually SHORT 3-month (90-day) redemption period for nonagricultural property, extended to 12 months for agricultural real estate, redemption price = bid + 10% annual interest), and Broker Responsibility and Office Management (14-16, largest state section, Broker-only -- real trust account rules requiring immediate/first-banking-day deposit and monthly 3-way reconciliation, and Wyoming's distinctive 'Funds Holder Agreement' mechanism (W.S. 33-28-102(b)(xxi)) -- a statutory alternative letting a broker use a Wyoming-licensed title company/closing agent/attorney to hold trust funds instead of maintaining the broker's own trust account, a real licensable substitute confirmed via WREC's own Responsible Broker application requirements). Governing law: W.S. Title 33, Chapter 28 (Real Estate License Act) and WREC's own 8 chapters of administrative rules. This bank was drafted across 5 new state-topic drafting passes (the 8 national files were reused, not redrafted). Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js.
